Tech Scan: Models

This page answers which model runs the work, and how typed decisions fit: approved Claude and OpenAI models through Amazon Bedrock, with the exceptions, exclusions and open gaps stated beside them.

This page is a draft. It covers model access, coding clients and typed decisions for the Concepts chapter. Its entries are research references from web sources reviewed 11–12 November 2026, not locally deployed or benchmarked options; treat vendor availability claims and public customer-reported operation as different kinds of evidence.

Read Choose an AI model in Concepts first. This page maps that section to products and does not repeat its explanation.

On this page
Purpose AWS-first default Conditional alternatives Research-only notes Do not use Gaps and open questions Sources

Purpose

Amazon Bedrock is the model API for this guide: approved Claude and OpenAI models are reached through Bedrock, and the coding clients that run the work connect to it there. This page records that default, the narrow exceptions to it, and the typed-decision models that are still research material rather than recommendations.

Apply hard gates first: required capability, approved data location and retention, identity and authorisation, supported model and API, security boundaries, and operational ownership. AWS preference must not override these gates. Among choices that pass the gates, prefer AWS-managed services.

Do not silently broaden the model policy through managed defaults, automatic routing, fallbacks, retrieval reasoning or evaluator models. A model that reaches the work through a default or a fallback is still a model choice, and it needs the same approval as a model chosen directly.

Offer one default and at most one justified alternative per capability in the main index. Keep further candidates in optional detail rather than presenting two complete parallel stacks; a reader choosing between two full stacks has not been given a decision.

Do not select the newest model merely because it is listed. Compare exact configurations on representative held-out tasks, and record correctness, correction effort, time, cost and control failures before choosing.[2]

Embedding and reranking models are approved separately from the generative models on this page. The model policy here covers large language models; extending that restriction to every model is an additional decision, not an assumption.

No option on this page has been locally deployed or benchmarked. Distinguish vendor availability claims from public customer-reported operation: a public customer case does not establish this team's performance or compliance, and a vendor availability claim does not establish that the option works for the proposed use.

AWS-first default

Use approved Claude and OpenAI models through Amazon Bedrock. Current official documentation includes frontier GPT models, not just GPT-OSS, and documents endpoint-specific API differences, so confirm the exact endpoint, region and features for the model you select.[1][3]

AWS-first default: models and coding clients
ProductWhat it doesStatusWhen to use it
Amazon Bedrock Model API for approved Claude and OpenAI models GA Default route for model access
Claude Code Coding client with documented Bedrock integration GA Default coding client through Bedrock
Codex Local coding client with documented Bedrock integration GA Default coding client through Bedrock

Claude Code and local Codex both have documented Bedrock integration.[5][4] Codex through Bedrock does not establish parity with Codex cloud or every hosted OpenAI feature; do not assume a feature available in the hosted service is available through Bedrock.

Managed GPT-OSS remains an OpenAI model and is not self-hosting. Omit it from the minimal shortlist if it is unnecessary, rather than saying the provider rule excludes it.

Bedrock access does not settle the qualification questions. Before adopting a selected model, qualify it in the intended account: representative task success, required model and API support, permission revocation, timeouts and retries, and full cost. These are proposed tests, not completed results.

Conditional alternatives

Direct provider APIs are exceptions, not the assumed route. Use a direct Claude or OpenAI API only for a specific capability or an approved-region gap, after reviewing egress, credentials, retention and data handling.[1]

The exception is narrow: it covers a specific capability or an approved-region gap, not a general preference for the provider API. Record the reason for the exception beside the choice, so a later reader can tell whether it still applies.

Conditional alternatives to the Bedrock default
ProductWhat it doesStatusWhen to use it
Direct Claude API Provider API for Claude models GA Exception only: a specific capability or approved-region gap
Direct OpenAI API Provider API for OpenAI models GA Exception only: a specific capability or approved-region gap
OpenAI Decisions API Typed predicate, choice and score answers; model gpt-6-luna GA Conditional direct-OpenAI evaluation only
Claude Platform on AWS Claude access as a third-party offering on AWS GA Conditional feature route only

The OpenAI Decisions API is documented as generally available with gpt-6-luna and native predicate, choice and score answers. No Box question is documented.[6] Treat it as a conditional direct-OpenAI evaluation: task accuracy, calibration, abstention and refusal handling, and application-side action checks are still required before any use.

Bedrock support for /decisions is not established. Availability of the same model through Responses does not prove availability of that API.[7]

Claude Platform on AWS is a conditional feature route, not interchangeable compliance evidence for Bedrock. AWS identifies it as a third-party offering outside standard AWS compliance programmes.[8]

Research-only notes

Decision models are now a category, not a single missing product. TypeSafe Jev, known in Concepts as System One, stays as educational material in Concepts; a deployment shortlist need not support every model family discussed there.[2] Do not present structured JSON as equivalent to a calibrated typed-decision model.

Research-only typed-decision models
ProductWhat it isStatusWhen to use it
TypeSafe Jev (System One) Hosted typed-decision model: Choice, Score, Noul, Box GA — launched 15 September 2026 Educational material only
Strands Decider 2B Open-weight typed-decision model: Choice, Score, Noul GA Not recommended; removed from the approved-stack recommendation

Strands Decider 2B is not recommended. The Decider experiment was removed from the approved-stack recommendation, and its JevBench numbers are the repository's own table, not settled results; do not quote them as a benchmark outcome. Decider documents only Choice, Score and Noul, with no Box equivalent.[9]

Cloudflare Clef and Clef-flash are the closest open-weight multimodal candidates, with a vision encoder for images and video, but their Box support is not confirmed. They are hosted on Cloudflare Workers AI, so they are out of scope for adoption and remain a research note only.[9]

Open-weight availability alone does not qualify a model. Decider is openly licensed and available, yet it stays out of the recommendation because its typed-decision coverage is incomplete and its reported accuracy is the repository's own table, not an independent result.

Other decision models named in the same research pass include Convai Laya, Liquid AI d1, Perplexity pplx-decider and Mapika decider-2b. None is recommended here.[9]

Do not use

These options are excluded from the recommended route. Exclusion is a decision about this guide's stack, not a judgement that the product itself is unusable elsewhere.

Excluded from the recommended route
ProductWhat it doesStatusWhen to use it
Self-hosted inference (vLLM, Ollama) Serves model weights on your own infrastructure GA Do not use: no model-weight hosting infrastructure is needed
Amazon SageMaker fine-tuning and model import Fine-tunes or imports models on SageMaker GA Do not use until a concrete requirement exists
Nova, Llama and Mistral generative models Generative models outside the approved Claude and OpenAI policy GA Do not use on the recommended route

No self-hosted inference infrastructure or non-Claude/OpenAI generative model is silently required by anything on this page. If a task appears to need one, treat that as a new decision with its own qualification, not as an implication of the recommended route. The exclusions are scoped to this guide's stack; they are not a ban on the products themselves.

Gaps and open questions

  • No Box support verified anywhere. No open-weight rival has been verified to document Box, visual grounding as a typed decision, and the OpenAI Decisions API documents no Box question.[9][6]
  • Bedrock support for /decisions is unresolved. Availability of the same model through Responses does not prove availability of that API.[7]
  • Claude Platform on AWS is not interchangeable compliance evidence for Bedrock. It is a third-party offering outside standard AWS compliance programmes, so a compliance case built on Bedrock cannot cite it.[8]
  • Nothing here is locally validated. Every entry is a research reference from web sources. Before adopting a selected model, qualify it in the intended account: representative task success, required model and API support, permission revocation, timeouts and retries, and full cost.
  • Model availability changes. A model listed today may later be retired or have its endpoint changed, so re-confirm the exact endpoint, region and features at adoption time rather than relying on this page's listing.[3]

Publishing a clearly labelled research reference does not itself mean the infrastructure has passed those tests. Keep existing human release and approval authority: updating this page does not authorise infrastructure deployment, repository migration, implementation, or issue closure.

What would close these gaps: a verified typed-decision model that documents Box, or a Bedrock announcement of /decisions support. Until then, typed visual-grounding decisions stay a human judgement, not a model call.

Next step: Compare the approved models on one representative held-out task — correctness, correction effort, time, cost and control failures — and record the result before adopting a model. The Harness spoke of Tech Scan covers the runtime that runs the chosen model.
